item.title: JVM Thread internals
item.description: A Java thread is one logical thread with three representations: the java.lang.Thread object a program creates, the HotSpot JavaThread the VM schedules and scans, and the operating system thread that actually runs. Such a thread owns a native stack, and carries a state word that the VM reads when it must stop the thread. A virtual thread keeps the first representation and drops the other two while it sits unmounted.
